questions.question: When and where did Thomas Hanrahan (born about 1840 in Ireland) marry Johanna Ryan (born about 1845 in Ireland)?
questions.rationale: The objective is a single marriage event and no question yet covers it. The couple's ties are already documented: the 1880 census shows them married in Saratoga, New York, and Irish baptisms for two children in 1871 and 1872 name both as parents. The tree records no marriage date or place. The first child on the tree was born in New York City in 1869, so the marriage most likely falls before that.

search_stop.justification: Researcher chose to wrap up q_001 before completing the plan. Evidence in hand: the 1880 Saratoga census shows Thomas and Johanna married with four US-born children, and an Irish Catholic parish register entry (src_004) records Thomam Hanrahan marrying Johan Ryan on 1 Feb 1868 at Ballylooby, County Tipperary — plausibly linked to the subject via the 1871/1872 Ardfinnan baptisms of their children, though the given names (Johan/Judy vs Johanna) are not an exact match and the link is marked probable, not confirmed. Completed searches: the Irish parish-register and marriage-index search that found the Ballylooby entry (pli_002); the 1865 and 1875 New York State censuses for Saratoga (pli_003), both negative; and a New York City marriage-records search 1858-1871 (pli_005), negative on the top 50 of 2,365 hits. Six plan items were not run at the researcher's request: FamilySearch hint review (blocked, tool disabled), Saratoga-area church marriage registers (only broader, non-targeted church-collection searches were logged), Tipperary civil registration 1864-1872, the Ardfinnan baptism register images, immigration/naturalization records, and death/burial records.

items.rationale: Tree facts: John Hanrahan baptised 28 Nov 1872 at Ardfinnan and Mary baptised 17 Feb 1871 in Ireland, both naming Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan as parents. The couple was therefore in Tipperary by 1871, so an Irish Catholic marriage is a strong candidate. Civil registration did not cover Catholic marriages before 1864 (loc_002), so before then only parish registers apply. Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900 is name-searchable; search Hanrahan/Hanrehan/Hanraghan/Hourigan with Ryan/Ryn and Johanna/Hanora/Joan/Julia variants, without a parish filter first, since loc_002 says Ardfinnan's own register volume was not located in the catalog and parish may rank rather than filter. Ireland, Marriages, 1619-1898 is name-searchable and is a second index.

The 1880 census shows Thomas (about 40) and Johanna (about 35) in Saratoga with four children said to be born in New York, but the tree also holds Irish baptisms for Mary (1871) and John (1872), so the census birthplaces and the baptisms conflict. The 1865 and 1875 New York State Censuses (both name-searchable) show where the couple lived and which children were with them, which tells us whether the marriage was before emigration or in New York. Per loc_001, each of these censuses has a marriage schedule after the population schedule, browsed by county and town; check it for a marriage in the year ending 1 June 1865 or 1875.

Per loc_001 there was no civil marriage registration in New York before 1880 and Catholic registers under the Diocese of Albany are the main source for an Irish Catholic couple. Search New York, Church Records, 1660-1954 and New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995 (both name-searchable) for Hanrahan and Ryan. The guide named no specific parish, so once step 3 fixes the town of residence, the parish register or Diocese of Albany archives must be approached directly. Include adjoining counties (Albany, Rensselaer, Washington, Warren), as the guide advises.
items.skip_reason: Researcher wrapped up q_001. Two Saratoga church/marriage searches (log_005, log_006) ran and were negative, but the log does not name a church register search, so the item could not be marked completed; closed as skipped.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Question
When and where did Thomas Hanrahan (born about 1840 in Ireland; living in Saratoga, New York, in 1880) marry Johanna Ryan (born about 1845 in Ireland)?

## Answer
A possible answer: they married on 1 February 1868 at Ballylooby, County Tipperary, Ireland. This is a possible finding, not a firm conclusion, because the one record that gives the date and place is an index entry whose link to this couple is only moderately supported and is in tension with the 1880 census.

## The record that gives an answer
The FamilySearch index of "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900" has an entry for "Thomam Hanrahan and Johan Ryan, 1 Feb 1868" at Ballylooby, County Tipperary (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6267-W22Q). It is an index (derivative) of a church register; the entry states the marriage directly and the parties are the informants of their own marriage, so the information is primary and direct. I have not read the register image. "Thomam" is the Latin accusative of Thomas and "Johan" a short form of Johanna, so the names fit; the surnames match exactly. The groom was linked to Thomas Hanrahan (KHGX-XWG) at probable (score 0.65) and the bride to Johanna Ryan (KC1J-LVB) at probable, but with a very low score (0.098) because the entry gives no age, parents or residence to compare. Those links rest on name variants and spousal fit, not on independent identifiers.

## Supporting context
Irish baptism entries for Mary (17 Feb 1871) and John (28 Nov 1872, Ardfinnan, Tipperary) name Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan as parents (FamilySearch, "Ireland, Births and Baptisms, 1620-1881"). Ardfinnan lies near Ballylooby, so a couple married at Ballylooby in 1868 and baptising children at Ardfinnan in 1871-72 is coherent. The 1880 census ("United States, Census, 1880", Saratoga, New York) shows Thomas (about 40, born Ireland, stone mason) and Johannah (about 35, born Ireland) with four children. No marriage in New York was found: the 1865 and 1875 state censuses for Saratoga and a partial New York City marriage search were negative. Statewide New York marriage registration did not begin until 1880, so a negative there is weak evidence either way.

## The tension that holds the tier down
The 1880 census gives all four children as born in New York, roughly 1864-65 (Mary), 1868-69 (Elizabeth), 1869-70 (Thomas) and 1871-72 (John). An 1868 marriage would postdate Mary's census-implied birth, and the Irish baptisms of a Mary in 1871 and a John in 1872 in Tipperary conflict with New York births for the same children in the same years. Either the census ages and birthplaces are loose, the family went back and forth, or the Tipperary couple and baptisms belong to a different Thomas and Johanna Hanrahan. These disagreements were not registered as formal conflicts, but they bear on whether the Ballylooby couple is the Saratoga couple, so they limit the answer to possible. The census was reported by an unknown household informant and is derivative; the baptism and marriage entries are also indexes. Nothing found contradicts the marriage entry itself, and no competing marriage record exists.

## What could settle it
The original Ballylooby marriage and Ardfinnan baptism register images (sponsors and residences); Irish civil registration for Tipperary 1864-1872; Catholic registers in the Diocese of Albany for Saratoga and neighbouring counties; immigration and naturalization records showing when Thomas arrived; and death or obituary records for either spouse.

## Tier
Possible. The 1 February 1868 Ballylooby date and place is the only candidate and is uncontradicted by any other marriage record, but identity with the Saratoga couple is not established. Proofs are never final; new evidence may change this.

# Locality Guide: Saratoga County, New York (1855-1875)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** February 7, 1791, from Albany County (FamilySearch Wiki, [Saratoga County, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy))
- **County seat:** Ballston Spa
- **Parent jurisdiction:** New York, United States
- **Population during period:** 51,729 (1860 census), 51,529 (1870 census) — flat growth in this window, per the FamilySearch Wiki county page
- **Economy:** Saratoga Springs' mineral-spring resort trade and Hudson River/canal-linked manufacturing and farming towns
- **Ethnic composition:** The wiki names large 19th-century Irish and other European Catholic immigration as the driver of Roman Catholic Church growth statewide; no Saratoga-County-specific ethnic breakdown was returned by these tools
- **Religious denominations present in the county (per NYGenWeb/FamilySearch Wiki):** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Presbyterian, Society of Friends (Quaker), and Roman Catholic (jurisdiction of the Diocese of Albany)
- **Key historical events affecting records:** none specific to this county and period were returned; no courthouse disaster is recorded for Saratoga County

## Boundary changes
Saratoga County's boundaries have been stable since its 1791 formation from Albany County; the FamilySearch Wiki's Boundary Changes section for the county names no later splits or annexations. No change affects records for 1855-1875.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date (level):** City/town/village — 1847 (law required but widely unenforced, compliance lapsing within a few years); State — 1880, general compliance for deaths by 1890 and births by 1913. (FamilySearch Wiki, [New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records))
- **What exists for 1855-1875:** No statewide marriage registration existed yet. The county-level page's own record-date chart independently gives marriage registration starting 1908 for Saratoga County, later than the state's general 1847/1880 framework — both figures come from the FamilySearch Wiki and are reported as given. In practice, a marriage occurring 1855-1875 is unlikely to have any surviving civil register entry.
- **Where held:** Town/village clerks for any surviving 1847-era entries; Saratoga County Clerk's office for any later county-held marriage records; New York State Department of Health for anything from 1880 forward.
- **Gaps:** The entire 1855-1875 window falls in the gap between the lapsed 1847 local law and the 1880 state system — civil marriage records very likely do not exist for this couple.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church marriage records (see Church records, below); the 1865 and 1875 New York State Census Marriage schedules (see Census records, below); newspaper marriage notices.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Presbyterian, Society of Friends, and Roman Catholic — per NYGenWeb's Saratoga Church Records page and the FamilySearch Wiki county page.
- **Catholic parishes:** Saratoga County parishes fall under the Diocese of Albany (FamilySearch Wiki, [New York Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Church_Records), Roman Catholic section). No tool result in this survey names the specific parish serving a particular Saratoga County town in 1855-1875, so no parish is recommended here; the [Local Catholic Church and Family History Genealogical Research Guide](https://freepages.rootsweb.com/~localcatholic/history/US-NewYorkNY.htm) cited by the wiki identifies New York parishes and their founding years and is the next place to check once the couple's town of residence is known.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials — standard Catholic parish registers; confirmations also kept separately.
- **Where held:** Original parish registers typically remain with the parish or have been transferred to the Diocese of Albany archives; FamilySearch's digitized Saratoga County church volumes located in this survey (Schuylerville Reformed Dutch Church marriages 1790-1857, Ballston Presbyterian marriages 1783-1865, Vischer Ferry Reformed Dutch marriages 1840-1855, Charlton Presbyterian marriages 1801-1862) are all Protestant congregations, not Catholic, so they do not cover this couple.
- **Gaps:** No Catholic parish marriage register for any Saratoga County town was found digitized or indexed by FamilySearch in this survey — this is a coverage gap, not evidence the register does not exist. Findmypast's "New York Roman Catholic Parish Marriages" and "New York Catholic Parish Registers Browse" collections (subscription) were named by the FamilySearch Wiki as covering Catholic parish marriages statewide and should be checked for Saratoga County coverage.
- **Language:** English expected for a New York Catholic parish of this era, though Latin sacramental formulas are typical in the register entries themselves.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1860 and 1870 federal censuses cover this window; federal mortality schedules for 1850-1880 (deaths in the 12 months before each census) are at Ancestry and on FS Library microfilm.
- **State census:** New York took state censuses in 1855, 1865, and 1875 — all three fall inside this window and are indexed with images at FamilySearch ("New York, State Census, 1855/1865/1875") and also at Ancestry.
- **Other enumerations:** The 1865 and 1875 state censuses each carry a Marriage schedule (and the 1865 also a Mortality and a Soldier Mortality schedule) recording events in the 12 months before the census, ending 1 June of the census year — found by browsing the images to the end of the town's population schedule. The marriage entry gives husband's and wife's names, ages, prior marital status, date and place of marriage, and whether it was a church or civil ceremony — a close match for this couple if their marriage fell in June 1864-May 1865 or June 1874-May 1875.
- **Access:** 1855/1865/1875 state censuses are indexed and image-searchable at FamilySearch; the marriage/mortality schedules are browse-only images at the end of each town's population schedule, not separately indexed by name.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories, petitions — held by the Surrogate Court per the FamilySearch Wiki county page.
- **Testate or intestate:** Unknown for this couple; check both will and administration series once a death date/place is known.
- **Date range:** From the county's 1791 formation; FamilySearch's digitized Saratoga probate volumes cover an 1799-1893 will index and 1909-1929 probate/guardianship/wills, per the volume survey.
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Surrogate Court; FS Library microfilm (e.g. Record of Wills Index 1799-1893, FS Library Film 555744) and FamilySearch digital images for parts of this material.
- **Relevance here:** Unlikely to name a marriage directly, but a later probate record for either spouse could confirm the marriage and name children.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not stated by the tools consulted for this county; New York generally used metes-and-bounds patents.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The FamilySearch Wiki's Land and Property section for Saratoga County names no specific granting office beyond directing researchers to the FamilySearch Catalog's Saratoga County land-records topic page.
- **Types:** Deeds, grants, patents — the volume survey found 68 Land-group volumes for this county and period, 33 full-text searchable, 8 browse-only, the rest unclassified by searchability.
- **Date range:** Earliest available not stated by these tools; FamilySearch's statewide "New York, Land Records, 1630-1975" collection (index & images) covers the period.
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Clerk's office (per the Courthouse section of the wiki page, which also handles marriage, divorce, court and land records); FamilySearch digitized images for part of the collection.
- **Relevance here:** A land deed naming "Thomas Hanrahan and wife Johanna" would confirm the marriage had occurred by that deed's date, even without finding the marriage record itself.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** The Civil War (1861-1865) falls inside this window.
- **Record types:** Town clerks' registers of Civil War soldiers (listing name, residence, birth date/place, parents' names, marital status, enlistment, discharge/death) exist for several Saratoga County towns — Ballston, Charlton, Clifton Park, Corinth, Edinburg, Galway, Greenfield, Halfmoon, Providence, Saratoga Springs, Stillwater, Waterford, Wilton — per the FamilySearch Wiki county page; originals are at the New York State Archives, microfilmed at FamilySearch (FS Library Film 1993401-37) and indexed at Ancestry.
- **Where held:** New York State Archives, Albany (originals); FamilySearch Library microfilm; Ancestry (index).
- **Relevance here:** If Thomas Hanrahan served, his town register entry could state his marital status and possibly his wife's name at a given date, bracketing the marriage.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** None named specifically for this couple by the tools consulted; county-wide cemetery indexes exist (see below).
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves both have county-level search pages for Saratoga County per the FamilySearch Wiki; FamilySearch's "New York, Cemetery Abstracts, 1800-1965" (index & images, 251,828 people) also covers the county.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held locally; the wiki names no specific Catholic cemetery for this county/period.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The Saratoga Sentinel (indexed for marriage/death notices 1819-1837, so just before this window) and the digital Saratogian index (1999-present, too late) are named by the FamilySearch Wiki county page; no newspaper index specifically covering 1855-1875 Saratoga County was found.
- **Where held:** Statewide marriage-notice indexes at Ancestry cover part of the window: "New York Marriage Notices" (1800-1855) and "New York Marriage Newspaper Extracts (Barber Collection)" (1801-1880) — the latter spans the full 1855-1875 period but is drawn from the Brooklyn Eagle and New York Evening Post, not Saratoga-local papers.
- **Content value:** A marriage or engagement notice could independently confirm date and place even without a parish or civil record.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Port of New York (the family's most likely port of arrival from Ireland, given the period).
- **Record types:** Passenger lists and naturalization records. FamilySearch's "US Famine Irish Passenger Index, 1846-1851" covers arrivals from Ireland just before this couple's likely immigration if they came during or just after the Famine; "New York, County Naturalization Records, 1791-1980" and "New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered, 1872-1878" both cover the window and could place Thomas Hanrahan in Saratoga County with a naturalization date.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (indexed & imaged for naturalizations); National Archives (passenger-list originals).
- **Content note:** Examine any located passenger manifest for the whole family group, not just Thomas or Johanna individually — infants and other relatives are listed alongside them.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property and personal tax assessment rolls — the FamilySearch Catalog lists an 1840 Saratoga County assessment roll; the volume survey found Legal/Land-group volumes that may include later tax material, but none was named specifically for 1855-1875 marriage-adjacent use.
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Clerk/Treasurer; FamilySearch Library microfilm for located rolls.
- **Substitute value:** Could place Thomas Hanrahan in a specific town in a given year, narrowing where to search for a parish, but was not confirmed by these tools to include marital-status detail.

### Other record types
- **Naturalization/voter records:** "New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered, 1872-1878" (FamilySearch, index & images) falls inside this window and could place Thomas Hanrahan in Saratoga County with a specific naturalization date and former residence/origin, useful corroborating evidence even though it does not record marriages.
- **County and town histories:** Cornell University's "Guide to Historical Resources in Saratoga County, New York Repositories" (1983) and Gordon Remington's "New York Towns, Villages, and Cities" guide are named by the FamilySearch Wiki as finding aids for locating further published/transcribed town records, including church and cemetery sources by town.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | New York, State Census 1855/1865/1875 (index & images); New York, County Marriages 1778-1848, 1908-1937 (index & images); New York, Church Records 1660-1954 (index & images, incomplete); New York, County Naturalization Records 1791-1980; New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered 1872-1878 | No statewide civil marriage registration exists for 1855-1875 — the state census marriage schedules and county/church marriage collections are the closest substitutes | Free |
| Findmypast | New York Roman Catholic Parish Marriages (index & images); New York Catholic Parish Registers Browse (images); New York State Religious Records 1716-1914 (images) | No digitized Catholic parish marriage register for Saratoga County was located on FamilySearch in this survey | Subscription |
| Ancestry | New York Marriage Newspaper Extracts (Barber Collection) 1801-1880 (index & images); New York State Census 1855/1865/1875; US Famine Irish Passenger Index 1846-1851 | Newspaper marriage notices and a dedicated Irish-arrivals index, neither held by FamilySearch | Subscription |
| NYGenWeb (saratoganygenweb.com) | Saratoga Church Records page (Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Society of Friends transcriptions, 1700s-1800s); Saratoga County Cemeteries index | Free county-level church/cemetery transcriptions outside the Catholic denomination | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 171 digitized volumes match Saratoga County for 1855-1875 per the volume search; the first page of up to 10 (returned with `summary: true`) is detailed above, and the rest were not examined individually — the by-record-type summary (e.g. 25 Marriage-group volumes, 11 browse-only and 8 full-text-only) covers all 171.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Saratoga County Clerk's office, Ballston Spa | Marriage, divorce, court and land records | In-person or mail request |
| Saratoga County Surrogate Court | Probate records | In-person or mail request |
| Saratoga County Historian, Ballston Spa | Obituaries, vital records, church records, maps, family files | Contact office; some search services offered |
| Saratoga County Historical Society (Brookside Museum), Ballston Spa | Surname files, local collections | In-person, or fee-based surname-file search |
| New York State Archives, Albany | Civil War town clerk registers; probate index copies | In-person or online request |
| Diocese of Albany archives | Catholic parish records for Saratoga County congregations (jurisdiction stated by FamilySearch Wiki; no specific parish or archive holdings confirmed by these tools) | Contact archive directly |

## Records NOT online
No Catholic parish marriage register for any Saratoga County town was found digitized, indexed, or image-browsable through FamilySearch in this survey — if such registers survive, they are very likely physical-only, held by the parish or the Diocese of Albany. Town clerk vital-record ledgers from the 1847-era local law (if any survive for Saratoga County towns) are not described as digitized by any tool here and would be physical-only at the town clerk's office. Saratoga County Surrogate Court probate case files outside the digitized will-index ranges are physical-only at the Surrogate Court or State Archives.

## Known record losses
No courthouse disaster or record loss is recorded for Saratoga County by the FamilySearch Wiki's Saratoga County Genealogy page ("There is no known history of courthouse disasters in this county"). The absence of a digitized Catholic marriage register for the county is a coverage/digitization gap, not a documented loss — no tool result states these registers were destroyed.

## Research tips
- Civil marriage registration did not reach the state level until 1880 (FamilySearch Wiki, [New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records)), so for a marriage dated 1855-1875 go straight to church records and census marriage schedules rather than expecting a civil certificate.
- Check the 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage schedules by browsing to the end of each candidate town's population schedule (FamilySearch Wiki county page, Census Records section) — these are browse-only, not name-indexed, so they must be paged through town by town.
- Saratoga County parishes are under the Diocese of Albany (FamilySearch Wiki, [New York Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Church_Records)); identify the couple's town of residence first, then use the Local Catholic Church and Family History Genealogical Research Guide to find which parish served that town in this period, since no tool result here pins a specific parish.
- Search the adjoining counties' Catholic parishes as well as Saratoga's own — Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, and Washington Counties all border Saratoga County (FamilySearch Wiki's Neighboring Counties table) and an Irish Catholic couple could easily have married in a larger parish just across a county line, particularly Albany (a major Diocese seat).
- Use "New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848; 1908-1937" and "New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995" at FamilySearch as broad statewide searches even though Saratoga-specific coverage for 1855-1875 was not confirmed — both are indexed and may surface an entry outside the gap years this county's own chart implies.
- If a marriage record cannot be found directly, pursue naturalization records (1872-1878 voter registration, county naturalization records) and land or probate records naming "Thomas Hanrahan and wife Johanna" to establish that the marriage had already occurred by a known date, narrowing the search window.

# Locality Guide: Ardfinnan, County Tipperary, Ireland (1855-1870)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** County Tipperary dates from the early 13th century, shortly after the Norman invasion of Ireland (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Tipperary; and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy).
- **County seat / administrative center:** the county has long been split administratively between North Tipperary (centred on Nenagh) and South Tipperary (centred on Clonmel); the two were reunited into one authority in 2012 (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy).
- **Parent jurisdiction:** province of Munster, Ireland.
- **Population during period:** 346,896 in 1821, rising to 435,553, then falling sharply after the Famine to 331,567 in 1851, and continuing to decline through the rest of the 19th century (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy). A direct population figure for the 1855-1870 window itself was not returned by this survey's population lookup (the tool could not resolve the place for that query).
- **Religious composition:** in 1871, 93.8% of the county's population was Roman Catholic, 5.4% Church of Ireland, and 0.3% each Presbyterian and Methodist (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy).
- **Key historical events affecting records:** the Great Famine (late 1840s) sharply reduced the population and disrupted record-keeping in the years just before this window; Catholic emancipation (1829) is the point after which most surviving Catholic parish registers begin (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).

## Boundary changes
- County Tipperary's own boundaries were stable through 1855-1870; what changed nationally in this window was civil registration machinery, not the county itself.
- Civil registration marriage districts were established covering the county from 1845 (non-Catholic only) and from 1864 (all marriages); these registration districts, not the older civil/Catholic parishes, are the unit by which civil marriage records are filed (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- Below the county, Ardfinnan is one of many Tipperary civil parishes; its own FamilySearch Wiki page carries no parish-specific record detail (see quirks).

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** marriage registration began nationally in 1845 for non-Catholic marriages only; it was extended to all marriages, and to births and deaths, in 1864 (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- **What exists:** "Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845-1913" (collection 2659409, index & images, 9,988,787 people) and "Ireland, Civil Registration Indexes, 1845-1958" (collection 1408347, index, 55,451,607 people) both cover the 1855-1870 window at FamilySearch.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (online, free); also IrishGenealogy.ie (index & images, marriages from 1845); General Register Office microfilm for 1864-1870 marriages is separately cataloged (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- **Gaps:** because Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan were apparently Catholic and the marriage is believed to predate 1865, it falls in the gap where civil registration did not yet cover Catholic marriages (pre-1864) — the civil index will show nothing for a pre-1864 Catholic marriage.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers (see Church records, below) are the primary source for a Catholic marriage before 1864.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic was overwhelmingly dominant in the county (93.8% in 1871); Church of Ireland, Presbyterian and Methodist congregations were also present in small numbers (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy).
- **Record types:** "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900" (collection 2820100, index & images, 27,172,041 people) covers baptisms, marriages and burials for this period; "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866" (collection 3460239, index) is a separate marriage-bond index.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds the indexed/imaged Catholic Parish Registers collection online; the underlying registers remain parish property, filmed by FamilySearch. volume_search found individually cataloged marriage/baptism microfilm volumes for specific Tipperary parishes in this window (e.g. Cloughjordan 1833-1858 and 1858-1881, Borrisokane 1844-1883, Moneygall/Cullenwaine 1820-1873) — but none of the returned coverage rows named Ardfinnan parish itself, so its register volume was not surfaced by this survey and must be located by a separate parish-name search of the catalog or collection.
- **Gaps:** most Catholic parish registers begin only around the time of emancipation (1829), so pre-1829 Catholic records are often absent; Ardfinnan's own register start date was not found by this survey.
- **Language:** Catholic registers of this period were commonly kept in Latin for sacramental entries (seen in nearby Tipperary volumes, e.g. "baptisms, marriages" noted with language codes en/la); expect some Latin terms even where the surrounding register is in English.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** only the 1901 and 1911 censuses for Ireland survive complete; all earlier 19th-century censuses, including any from the 1855-1870 window, were destroyed or survive only in fragments (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Getting_Started and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Tipperary,_Ireland_Genealogy, which lists only 1901 and 1911 collections for the county).
- **State/provincial census:** none found for this county and period.
- **Other enumerations:** Griffith's Valuation (1847-1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1824-1855) are the standard substitutes for a missing census in this era; see Land records below.
- **Access:** the 1901/1911 Ireland censuses are indexed & images online at FamilySearch; no online census coverage exists for 1855-1870.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** wills, administrations, probate and marriage-license bonds were handled through diocesan consistory courts in this period; the Diocese of Cashel and Emly's consistory court covered 118 parishes in County Tipperary.
- **Testate or intestate:** unknown for Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan at this stage; a will would be sought via the wills indexes, an administration via the administrations indexes, if no will is known to exist.
- **Date range:** "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Wills & Administrations Indexes" covers 1595-1858; "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes" covers 1623-1866 and is directly relevant to a pre-1864 marriage search.
- **Where held:** originals were at the Public Record Office, Dublin, per catalog note on the Diocese of Cashel and Emly act books (catalog entry koha:158619); FamilySearch holds microfilm copies, some online.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** metes and bounds, as administered through the Valuation Office and Griffith's Valuation survey process.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** the Valuation Office (Dublin) produced both the earlier Valuation Office Books and Griffith's Valuation; this survey's wiki page did not name a separate land-grant authority for Tipperary.
- **Types:** "Ireland, Valuation Office Books, 1831-1856" (collection 2329951, index & images, 13,485,480 people) and Griffith's Valuation, 1847-1864 (named in the county wiki page, held at MyHeritage/Ancestry, index & images, subscription).
- **Date range:** 1824-1864 across these two land-valuation series, overlapping the early part of the 1855-1870 window.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (Valuation Office Books, free); Griffith's Valuation itself is on MyHeritage and Ancestry (subscription) and on Ask About Ireland (free index only, per the external-links results).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** no Irish conflict fell within 1855-1870 itself; the Crimean War (1853-1856) and later British Army service are the nearest-period conflicts that could have drawn in a man of Thomas Hanrahan's generation, though this survey found no Tipperary-specific record of such service.
- **Record types:** "Ireland, Merchant Navy Crew Lists, 1857-1922" overlaps this window if a maritime occupation is suspected; otherwise general British Army service records (1760-1915) are listed among the external links for the county.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (Merchant Navy Crew Lists, online); British Army records via Findmypast (subscription), per the external-links results.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** none named specifically for Ardfinnan or Thomas Hanrahan/Johanna Ryan by any tool result in this survey.
- **Online coverage:** Find a Grave's Ireland cemetery index and the Ireland Cemetery Collection, 1865-2023 (Ancestry, index only) both overlap the tail of this window.
- **Physical records:** none identified by this survey for this specific locality; a local sexton or parish burial register would need to be checked directly.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The Cork Examiner (1841-1871) and The Freeman's Journal (1800-1949) are both indexed at Findmypast and could carry Tipperary notices in this window, per the external-links results.
- **Where held:** Findmypast (subscription, images); no free online Tipperary-specific newspaper archive was returned by this survey.
- **Content value:** marriage, birth and death notices, useful as a substitute lead when register entries are not found.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** the family is known to have emigrated to the United States (Saratoga, New York by 1880); Irish emigration in this era commonly left through Cork (Queenstown/Cobh) or Liverpool.
- **Record types:** "Irish Passenger Lists, 1847-1871" (Ancestry, images only) and "Ireland and Britain, Transatlantic Migration from North America, 1858-1870" (FamilySearch collection 3499249) both fall inside this window.
- **Where held:** Ancestry (subscription, images); FamilySearch (free, for the transatlantic-migration collection).
- **Content note:** passenger manifests list every person aboard including children, so if the couple emigrated together or with children, check the full manifest, not just the named head of household.

### Tax records
- **Types:** the Tithe Applotment Books (1814-1855, FamilySearch collection 1804886, 753,820 people) and the Valuation Office Books (1831-1856) serve as the main substitute tax/property records for this county and period.
- **Date range:** both end at or just before 1855-1856, so they mainly document the years immediately preceding this window rather than inside it.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (both, free, index & images); the Tithe Applotment Books are also at the National Archives of Ireland online (free, images only).
- **Substitute value:** useful for placing the Hanrahan and Ryan families on the land just before the suspected marriage date, in the absence of a census.

### Other record types
- National School Registers, 1847-1954 (FamilySearch collection 4496116, 104,149 people) could record children of the couple if they were of school age within the county before emigration.

## Research tips
- Because the marriage is believed to predate 1865 and the couple was apparently Catholic, search the Catholic Parish Registers collection (and the Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866) before the civil marriage index, which will be empty for a pre-1864 Catholic marriage (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- Civil marriage registers, once they do apply (1864 onward), record the names and occupations of both fathers and the denomination of the church where the marriage occurred — useful for confirming parentage once a civil-era record is found (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- "Marriages were usually performed in the bride's parish" per the civil registration guidance — so if Johanna Ryan's home parish differs from Ardfinnan (where a child was later baptised), search that parish's registers for the marriage itself, not only Ardfinnan's (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- Civil registration districts cover many villages at once and do not align with parish boundaries, so use John Grenham's place-search tool or the S. Wilson registration-district map to confirm which district and parishes correspond to Ardfinnan before assuming a search is complete (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration).
- Because no census survives for this county before 1901, use Griffith's Valuation and the Valuation Office Books to place the Hanrahan and Ryan households in the Ardfinnan area in the years just before the marriage.
- Ardfinnan's own FamilySearch Wiki page carries no parish-specific detail, so search the Catholic Parish Registers collection directly by parish name ("Ardfinnan") rather than relying on that page.
